          (symmetricRectangleLower R c) (symmetricRectangleUpper R c) =

  let z₂ := symmetricRectangleUpper R c
  have hzre : z₁.re < z₂.re := by
    dsimp only [z₁, z₂]
    simp [symmetricRectangleLower, symmetricRectangleUpper]
    linarith
  have hzim : z₁.im < z₂.im := by
    dsimp only [z₁, z₂]
    simp [symmetricRectangleLower, symmetricRectangleUpper]
    linarith
  have hbottom : ∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc z₁.re z₂.re,
      XiExplicitAdmissible ((x : ℂ) + z₁.im * I) := by
    intro x hx
    have hx' : x ∈ Set.uIcc (-R) R := by
      simpa [z₁, z₂, symmetricRectangleLower, symmetricRectangleUpper] using hx
    simpa [z₁, symmetricRectangleLower, sub_eq_add_neg] using! hadm.1 x hx'
  have htop : ∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc z₁.re z₂.re,
      XiExplicitAdmissible ((x : ℂ) + z₂.im * I) := by
    intro x hx
    have hx' : x ∈ Set.uIcc (-R) R := by
      simpa [z₁, z₂, symmetricRectangleLower, symmetricRectangleUpper] using hx
    simpa [z₂, symmetricRectangleUpper] using hadm.2.1 x hx'
  have hright : ∀ y ∈ Set.uIcc z₁.im z₂.im,
      XiExplicitAdmissible ((z₂.re : ℂ) + y * I) := by
    intro y hy
    have hy' : y ∈ Set.uIcc (-c) c := by
      simpa [z₁, z₂, symmetricRectangleLower, symmetricRectangleUpper] using hy
    simpa [z₂, symmetricRectangleUpper] using hadm.2.2.1 y hy'
  have hleft : ∀ y ∈ Set.uIcc z₁.im z₂.im,
      XiExplicitAdmissible ((z₁.re : ℂ) + y * I) := by
    intro y hy
    have hy' : y ∈ Set.uIcc (-c) c := by
      simpa [z₁, z₂, symmetricRectangleLower, symmetricRectangleUpper] using hy
    simpa [z₁, symmetricRectangleLower] using hadm.2.2.2 y hy'

    rectIntegral_continuedPrimeArchSourceRelativeTrace_eq_closedRectangleZeroSum

      hzre hzim hbottom htop hright hleft

    apply mul_ne_zero

by
  have hm :
      Multipliable (fun n : {n // n ∉ S} =>
        RHTower.weierstrassE1
          (z / (movingCanonicalZero θ n.1 : ℂ))) :=
    RHTower.canonicalProductE1IndexedComplement_multipliable
      (fun n => (movingCanonicalZero θ n : ℂ))
      (fun n => n ∈ S)
      (fun n => Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr
        (ne_of_gt (movingCanonicalZero_pos θ n)))
      (summable_movingCanonicalZero_inv_sq θ) z
  change
    (∏' n : {n // n ∉ S},
      RHTower.weierstrassE1
        (conj z /
          (movingCanonicalZero θ n.1 : ℂ))) =
      conj
        (∏' n : {n // n ∉ S},
          RHTower.weierstrassE1
            (z /
              (movingCanonicalZero θ n.1 : ℂ)))
  calc
    (∏' n : {n // n ∉ S},
        RHTower.weierstrassE1
          (conj z /
            (movingCanonicalZero θ n.1 : ℂ))) =
      ∏' n : {n // n ∉ S},
        Complex.conjAe.toMonoidHom
          (RHTower.weierstrassE1
            (z /
              (movingCanonicalZero θ n.1 : ℂ))) := by
        apply tprod_congr
        intro n
        change
          RHTower.weierstrassE1
              (conj z /
                (movingCanonicalZero θ n.1 : ℂ)) =
            conj
              (RHTower.weierstrassE1
                (z /

        simp only [RHTower.weierstrassE1,
          map_mul, map_sub, map_one, map_div₀,
          Complex.conj_ofReal]
        rw [← Complex.exp_conj]
        rw [map_div₀, Complex.conj_ofReal]
    _ = Complex.conjAe.toMonoidHom
        (∏' n : {n // n ∉ S},
          RHTower.weierstrassE1
            (z /

## Zero-divisor-preserving variant and its cost `[PROVED HERE]`

Hermite interpolation also gives a real-even polynomial `Q` with

`Q'(a)=-F'(a)/F(a)`                                          (10)

`H=e^Q F`                                                     (11)

Hypertranscendence versus differential algebraicity is unchanged by the zero-free DA multiplier.

The cost is growth: in general `e^Q` has order `deg Q`.  Arbitrary interpolation therefore leaves

## Order-one fixed-divisor rigidity `[PROVED, CLASSICAL]`

Let `F` and `G` be nonzero entire functions of order at most one with the same zeros and
multiplicities.  Hadamard factorization gives

`G(z)/F(z)=exp(az+b)`                                        (13)

for constants `a,b`.  If both functions are even, (13) at `z` and `-z` forces `a=0`.  If both are
Schwarz-real, the remaining constant is real and nonzero.  With one common normalization value,
`F=G`.

Thus the simultaneous cage

`fixed divisor + order one + FE-evenness + one normalization` (14)

has no zero-free gauge freedom.  Critical-point plasticity survives exact order through polynomial
gauges only by changing the divisor; it preserves the divisor only by paying additional growth.
This is the precise boundary at which a canonical Speiser-type statement can become meaningful.

## Exact route consequence

Speiser proved that RH is equivalent to the absence of nonreal zeros of `zeta'` in the left half of
the critical strip.  The results above prove:

1. no finite Speiser packet can be derived from an unpointed HT field, differential matroid, or

2. even exact order one and scalar FE/Schwarz symmetry do not repair this finite blindness when
   polynomial divisor gauges are allowed;
3. HT plus the complete zero divisor still does not determine critical points if the order-one
   normalization is dropped;
4. only the canonical order-one fixed-divisor representative removes both gauge freedoms.

This does **not** refute Speiser's theorem or exclude a proof using its full half-strip condition for
the canonical Riemann zeta function.  It excludes implementations that expect HT structure, finite
critical-point verification, or an unpointed field/pro-field to supply the missing localization.
The surviving route must use the exact Euler-normalized representative and global critical-point

/-!
# Speiser's sign law on the critical line

The functional equation gives the exact critical-line identity
`2 Re(ζ'/ζ)(1/2+it) = log π − Re ψ(1/4 + it/2)` (`re_logDeriv_riemannZeta_criticalLine`), and the
digamma real part exceeds `log π` from height `20` on (`log_pi_lt_re_digamma_quarter`).  Hence
`Re(ζ'/ζ) < 0` on the critical line above that height wherever `ζ ≠ 0`.  Consequences:

* `deriv_riemannZeta_criticalLine_ne_zero_of_ne_zero` — `ζ'` does not vanish at any non-zero of
  `ζ` on the line above height `20`;
* `riemannZeta_criticalLine_eq_zero_of_deriv_eq_zero` — a critical point of `ζ` on the critical
  line above height `20` is a (multiple) zero of `ζ`.

This is the reflection-odd orientation law that drives Speiser's theorem (`RH ⟺ ζ' has no zeros in
`0 < Re s < 1/2`): on the line the logarithmic derivative points into the left half-plane, so the
argument of `ζ'/ζ` cannot wind along the critical line.  The law is unconditional and contains no
zero of `ζ`; Speiser's equivalence itself is a receiver.
-/

open Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- **Speiser's sign law.**  Above height `20`, `Re(ζ'/ζ) < 0` on the critical line wherever
`ζ ≠ 0`. -/
theorem re_logDeriv_riemannZeta_criticalLine_neg {τ : ℝ} (hτ : 20 ≤ τ)
    (hz : riemannZeta (1 / 2 + (τ : ℂ) * I) ≠ 0) :
    (logDeriv riemannZeta (1 / 2 + (τ : ℂ) * I)).re < 0 := by
  have hid := re_logDeriv_riemannZeta_criticalLine (t := τ) hz
  have hdig := log_pi_lt_re_digamma_quarter hτ
  have hcast : (((1 / 4 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((τ / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * I) = 1 / 4 + (τ : ℂ) * I / 2 := by
    push_cast; ring
  rw [hcast] at hdig
  linarith

/-- On the critical line above height `20`, `ζ'` does not vanish where `ζ` does not. -/
theorem deriv_riemannZeta_criticalLine_ne_zero_of_ne_zero {τ : ℝ} (hτ : 20 ≤ τ)
    (hz : riemannZeta (1 / 2 + (τ : ℂ) * I) ≠ 0) :
    deriv riemannZeta (1 / 2 + (τ : ℂ) * I) ≠ 0 := by
  intro hd
  have h := re_logDeriv_riemannZeta_criticalLine_neg hτ hz
  rw [logDeriv_apply, hd, zero_div] at h
  simp at h

/-- **Critical points on the critical line are multiple zeros.**  Above height `20`, a zero of
`ζ'` on the line is a zero of `ζ`. -/
theorem riemannZeta_criticalLine_eq_zero_of_deriv_eq_zero {τ : ℝ} (hτ : 20 ≤ τ)
    (hd : deriv riemannZeta (1 / 2 + (τ : ℂ) * I) = 0) :
    riemannZeta (1 / 2 + (τ : ℂ) * I) = 0 := by
  by_contra hz
  exact deriv_riemannZeta_criticalLine_ne_zero_of_ne_zero hτ hz hd

end

end RHTower

At finitely many distinct regular points of an analytic function, one polynomial multiplier can
force the derivative of the product to vanish simultaneously.  The load-bearing step is the

    (f df : ι → ℂ) (hf : ∀ i, f i ≠ 0) :
    ∃ P : Polynomial ℂ, ∀ i,
      P.eval (w i) = 1 ∧
      (derivative P).eval (w i) * f i + P.eval (w i) * df i = 0 := by

    exists_polynomial_iterateDerivative_eval_eq w hw (fun _ => 2) target

  have h0 := hP i 0 (by omega)

  have hP1 : (derivative P).eval (w i) = -df i / f i := by
    simpa [target] using h1
  refine ⟨hP0, ?_⟩

/-- **The gauge factorizes through every translate and every power.**  This is the identity that
lets a polynomial gauge be absorbed into the rational base field of a translation family. -/
theorem translate_pow_polynomial_mul (P : Polynomial ℂ) (F : ℂ → ℂ) (h : ℂ) (N : ℕ) (z : ℂ) :
    ((fun w => P.eval w * F w) (z + h)) ^ N
      = (P.comp (X + C h)).eval z ^ N * (F (z + h)) ^ N := by
  have hcomp : (P.comp (X + C h)).eval z = P.eval (z + h) := by
    rw [Polynomial.eval_comp]
    simp
  rw [hcomp, mul_pow]

/-- The gauge factor is a nonzero element of the rational base: the translate of a nonzero
polynomial is nonzero, hence so is each of its powers. -/
theorem translate_pow_ne_zero {P : Polynomial ℂ} (hP : P ≠ 0) (h : ℂ) (N : ℕ) :
    (P.comp (X + C h)) ^ N ≠ 0 := by
  refine pow_ne_zero N ?_
  intro hzero
  apply hP
  have hback : (P.comp (X + C h)).comp (X - C h) = P := by
    rw [Polynomial.comp_assoc]
    simp
  rw [hzero] at hback
  simpa using hback.symm

/-- **The polynomial factor costs no order.**  Multiplying an entire function carrying the
order-one envelope by any polynomial leaves the same envelope with a larger constant. -/
theorem orderOneEnvelope_mul_polynomial {F : ℂ → ℂ} {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C) (P : Polynomial ℂ)
    (hbound : ∀ z : ℂ, ‖F z‖ ≤ Real.exp (C * (1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖))) :
    ∃ C' : ℝ, 0 ≤ C' ∧
      ∀ z : ℂ, ‖P.eval z * F z‖ ≤ Real.exp (C' * (1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖)) := by
  set A : ℝ := polynomialCoeffNormSum P with hA
  have hAnn : 0 ≤ A := by
    rw [hA, polynomialCoeffNormSum]
    positivity
  have hlog2 : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log 2 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)
  set d : ℕ := P.natDegree with hd
  set C₁ : ℝ := A / Real.log 2 + d with hC₁
  have hC₁nn : 0 ≤ C₁ := by positivity
  refine ⟨C + C₁, by linarith, fun z => ?_⟩
  have hr0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖z‖ := norm_nonneg z
  have hlogle : Real.log 2 ≤ Real.log (2 + ‖z‖) :=
    Real.log_le_log (by norm_num) (by linarith)
  have hLpos : 0 < Real.log (2 + ‖z‖) := lt_of_lt_of_le hlog2 hlogle
  have hbase : Real.log 2 ≤ (1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖) := by nlinarith
  -- the coefficient sum
  have hAle : A ≤ Real.exp (A / Real.log 2 * ((1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖))) := by
    refine le_trans (by linarith [Real.add_one_le_exp A]) (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr ?_)
    have hdiv : 0 ≤ A / Real.log 2 := by positivity
    have : A / Real.log 2 * Real.log 2 ≤ A / Real.log 2 * ((1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖)) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbase hdiv
    rw [div_mul_cancel₀ _ hlog2.ne'] at this
    exact this
  -- the degree power
  have hpow : (1 + ‖z‖) ^ d ≤ Real.exp ((d : ℝ) * ((1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖))) := by
    have hbasepos : (0 : ℝ) < 1 + ‖z‖ := by linarith
    have hexp : (1 + ‖z‖) ^ d = Real.exp ((d : ℝ) * Real.log (1 + ‖z‖)) := by
      rw [Real.exp_nat_mul, Real.exp_log hbasepos]
    rw [hexp]
    refine Real.exp_le_exp.mpr ?_
    have h1 : Real.log (1 + ‖z‖) ≤ Real.log (2 + ‖z‖) :=
      Real.log_le_log (by linarith) (by linarith)
    have h2 : Real.log (2 + ‖z‖) ≤ (1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖) := by nlinarith
    have h3 : Real.log (1 + ‖z‖) ≤ (1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖) := le_trans h1 h2
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h3 (Nat.cast_nonneg d)
  have hPle : ‖P.eval z‖ ≤ A * (1 + ‖z‖) ^ d := norm_polynomial_eval_le P z
  have hprod : A * (1 + ‖z‖) ^ d ≤ Real.exp (C₁ * ((1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖))) := by
    have := mul_le_mul hAle hpow (by positivity) (Real.exp_nonneg _)
    rw [← Real.exp_add] at this
    refine le_trans this (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr ?_)
    rw [hC₁]
    ring_nf
    exact le_refl _
  rw [norm_mul]
  calc ‖P.eval z‖ * ‖F z‖
      ≤ (A * (1 + ‖z‖) ^ d) * Real.exp (C * (1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖)) :=
        mul_le_mul hPle (hbound z) (norm_nonneg _) (by positivity)
    _ ≤ Real.exp (C₁ * ((1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖)))
        * Real.exp (C * (1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖)) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hprod (Real.exp_nonneg _)
    _ = Real.exp ((C + C₁) * (1 + ‖z‖) * Real.log (2 + ‖z‖)) := by
        rw [← Real.exp_add]
        congr 1
        ring

/-
# The entire regularized determinant of the theta source pencil

The corpus determinant `thetaFredholmDet` is the disc-local exponential representative
`exp(−∑_{n≥2} zⁿ/n·tr(Bⁿ))`, nowhere zero by construction.  Its analytic continuation to the whole
plane is the Hilbert–Carleman determinant, and *that* is the object whose divisor the card's
determinant clause is about.

Here the general construction is instantiated at the actual arithmetic source: `thetaEntireDet2`
is entire, equals `thetaFredholmDet` near the origin, takes the value one there, is the unique such
function, and each of its nonzero zeros is a reciprocal eigenvalue of the source inverse itself.

Main results:
* `thetaEntireDet2`, `differentiable_thetaEntireDet2`, `isRegularizedDet_thetaEntireDet2`.
* `thetaEntireDet2_eq_thetaFredholmDet` — the agreement near the origin.
* `exists_eigenvector_of_thetaEntireDet2_eq_zero` — its zeros are reciprocal eigenvalues.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Hedenmalm.HedenmalmThetaTrace
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.RegularizedDeterminantEigenvalueLimit

namespace RHTower

namespace HedenmalmThetaSource

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry HilbertSchmidt MeasureTheory

/-- **The entire regularized determinant of the source pencil.** -/
noncomputable def thetaEntireDet2 : ℂ → ℂ := entireDet2 thetaKernelMatrix

theorem differentiable_thetaEntireDet2 : Differentiable ℂ thetaEntireDet2 :=
  differentiable_entireDet2 isHS_thetaKernelMatrix

theorem isRegularizedDet_thetaEntireDet2 :
    IsRegularizedDet thetaKernelMatrix thetaEntireDet2 :=
  isRegularizedDet_entireDet2 isHS_thetaKernelMatrix

theorem thetaEntireDet2_zero : thetaEntireDet2 0 = 1 :=
  isRegularizedDet_thetaEntireDet2.eq_one_at_zero

/-- **Uniqueness.**  Any entire function agreeing with the local determinant near the origin is
`thetaEntireDet2`. -/
theorem eq_thetaEntireDet2_of_isRegularizedDet {D : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hD : IsRegularizedDet thetaKernelMatrix D) : D = thetaEntireDet2 :=
  hD.unique isRegularizedDet_thetaEntireDet2

/-- The entire determinant agrees with the corpus disc-local determinant near the origin. -/
theorem thetaEntireDet2_eq_thetaFredholmDet :
    ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ z ∈ Metric.ball (0 : ℂ) r, thetaEntireDet2 z = thetaFredholmDet z := by
  obtain ⟨-, r, hr, -, he⟩ := isRegularizedDet_thetaEntireDet2
  exact ⟨r, hr, he⟩

/-- The represented operator of the kernel matrix is the coordinate model of the source
inverse. -/
theorem toOperator_thetaKernelMatrix :
    toOperator isHS_thetaKernelMatrix = thetaKernelMatrixOperator :=
  toOperator_matrixOf isHilbertSchmidt_thetaKernelMatrixOperator

/-- **A zero of the entire theta determinant is a reciprocal eigenvalue of the source inverse.**
The transport is through the coordinate isometry of the quantile space onto `ℓ²`. -/
theorem exists_eigenvector_of_thetaEntireDet2_eq_zero {z₀ : ℂ} (hz₀ : z₀ ≠ 0)
    (h : thetaEntireDet2 z₀ = 0) :
    ∃ f : Lp ℂ 2 unitIntervalMeasure, f ≠ 0 ∧ thetaKernelOperator f = z₀⁻¹ • f := by
  obtain ⟨w, hw0, hw⟩ :=
    exists_eigenvector_of_entireDet2_eq_zero isHS_thetaKernelMatrix hz₀ h
  rw [toOperator_thetaKernelMatrix] at hw
  refine ⟨thetaCoord.symm w, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hzero
    exact hw0 (by simpa using congrArg thetaCoord hzero)
  · have hcoord : thetaCoord (thetaKernelOperator (thetaCoord.symm w)) = z₀⁻¹ • w := by
      simpa [thetaKernelMatrixOperator] using hw
    have := congrArg thetaCoord.symm hcoord
    simpa [map_smul] using this

end HedenmalmThetaSource
